about: The math film's script: what stretto estimates, why a flow is safe, the rule that decides a lookup, the counts behind it, alpha's posterior as a fugue program, the argument bindings, calibration and the audit. Chapters (`beats`) of lines, as the explainer's: `text` is the caption, `say` what the voice says, `em` the phrases lit in petrol, `post` the pause after a line. Every formula is the paper's (paper/stretto.md) or the code's, and every number has its scope on screen. narrate.py voices it (math-video).

lines.text: The math inside stretto, as the code computes it.
One event to estimate, one rule to act on it, and the counts between.
A lookup pays off if the agent uses it before its next write.
So stretto estimates q: the chance a read is among those the agent makes before it writes.
That chance is at least the chance the read comes next, and often far larger.
After a user's details, the habit put an order next at 0.64. The agents read one before the write 94% of the time.
lines.say: After a user's details, the habit put an order next at zero point six four. The agents read one before the write ninety-four percent of the time.

lines.text: A flow makes only reads, and reads leave the state as it was.
If the agent makes the same calls, every write lands on the same state.
A wrong lookup changes only what the agent reads. Its worst case is a detour.
Used, a lookup saves a turn, worth beta. Unused, it costs a detour, delta.
Its expected value is q times beta, minus one minus q, times delta.
That's positive exactly when q clears delta over beta plus delta.
Live on τ²-bench, beta was about 6,000 input tokens and delta about 2,530.
lines.say: Live on tau two bench, beta was about six thousand input tokens, and delta about twenty-five thirty.

lines.text: So the line sits at about 0.3. In airline and telecom, the counts put it lower.
lines.say: So the line sits at about zero point three. In airline and telecom, the counts put it lower.

lines.text: The chances come from counts. Each step becomes its tool, its outcome, and a feature of its result.
A back-off model predicts the next step from the last two.
Each context is a Dirichlet–multinomial, with the shorter context as its prior mean.
lines.say: Each context is a Dirichlet multinomial, with the shorter context as its prior mean.
em: the shorter context as its prior mean.

lines.text: For the reach decider, the same contexts count each read used before the next write.
Alpha sets how fast the counts outweigh the prior. It isn't tuned by hand.
It's inferred, with fugue, a probabilistic programming library for Rust.
The program draws log alpha from a normal prior, and scores the episodes, one step at a time.
Metropolis–Hastings samples the posterior, and the flow keeps its median.
lines.say: Metropolis Hastings samples the posterior, and the flow keeps its median.

lines.text: A lookup also needs its arguments. stretto counts where each one came from.
A binding's chance is right over tried, shrunk toward one half.
The decision multiplies the two: the read's chance, times its arguments'.
Counting the right event calibrates the probability of use.
In replay, its calibration error was 0.01 to 0.08 in every τ²-bench domain.
lines.say: In replay, its calibration error was zero point zero one to zero point zero eight in every tau two bench domain.

lines.text: Scored on the next step instead, it was 0.06 to 0.16.
lines.say: Scored on the next step instead, it was zero point zero six to zero point one six.

lines.text: A flow is audited as a program too.
Each decision is a categorical choice at its own address: a lookup, handing back, or another step.
fugue scores the agent's real path under it, in nats of surprise per decision.
The paper gives the proofs and the benchmark numbers. The worked examples are the walkthrough's.
em: the proofs and the benchmark numbers.
